Reportedly, Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, indicating that this cooling technology is set to play a more important role in future hardware product lines. Details as follows.

Apple Doubles Down on Vapor Chamber Cooling Technology

A Weibo leaker account named "定焦數碼" posted that Apple has "substantially increased its total vapor chamber orders," and speculated that the move "may be to prepare more powerful cooling solutions for its first foldable iPhone and next year's anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helps address the overheating issues that have persisted over the past several generations.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location to spread the heat over a larger area, before letting the liquid flow back and repeating the cycle.

To see the whole process, check out this brilliant video produced by Know Art:

Although the Weibo post speculated that Apple's increased procurement this time is for the iPhone Ultra and the rumored anniversary edition iPhone expected in 2027, looking at the timeline, it is actually more reasonable that this year's product line adopts this technology first.

According to reports, Apple has asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the earlier target of 7 to 8 million units. At the same time, the company has also stockpiled around 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

Along with the increase in orders, there are also reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and yield issues, clearing obstacles for ramping up production ahead of the September launch.
